facts.statement: Tristychius was a small animal reaching a maximum length of about 60 cm.
facts.quote: Tristychius was a small animal, up to about 60 cm long.

facts.statement: Tristychius possessed a heterocercal tail fin and large spines on its two dorsal fins.
facts.quote: It had a heterocercal caudal fin, and large spines on two dorsal fins.

facts.statement: Tristychius had only two basal plates on its pectoral fin, lacking the mesopterygium found in other chondrichthyans.
facts.quote: Unlike other chondrichthyans that have three basal plates on pectoral fin (propterygium, mesopterygium and metapterygium), its pectoral fin had only two basal plates and lacked mesopterygium.

facts.statement: Tristychius is estimated to have been a specialized suction-feeding benthic predator that likely ambushed or stealthily approached its prey.
facts.quote: it is estimated to be a specialized suction feeding benthic predator, either ambushing or using stealth to approach its prey.

facts.statement: Fossils of the only known species, Tristychius arcuatus, including fin spines, have been discovered in Scotland.
facts.quote: Fossils of T. arcuatus, the type and only species, including fin spines have been found in Scotland.

facts.statement: Although historically classified as a hybodont, a 2016 study reclassified Tristychius as a basal euselachian, noting that hybodonts are more closely related to modern sharks and rays.
facts.quote: While historically considered a hybodont, a 2016 study considered it to be a basal euselachian, with hybodonts more closely related to Neoselachii (the group of modern sharks and rays) than to Tristychius.

facts.statement: Tristychius is placed in the family Tristychiidae alongside the genus Acronemus.
facts.quote: The study placed the genus in the family Tristychiidae along with Acronemus.

facts.statement: Tristychius lived during the Visean to Serpukhovian stages, between 346.7 and 326.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Visean to Serpukhovian (346.7 to 326.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tristychius belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
There are 9 recorded fossil occurrences of Tristychius in the Paleobiology Database.
The genus Tristychius was described by Agassiz in 1837.

rejected.statement: Tristychius is an extinct genus of euselachian cartilaginous fish from the Carboniferous period.
rejected.quote: Tristychius (from Greek, 'three' and 'row') is an extinct genus of euselachian chondrichthyan from the Carboniferous period (Visean).
